title_en: Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on the Publication of Judicial Documents by People's Courts on the Internet

articles.content_en: Article 1 When publishing adjudicative documents on the Internet, the People's Court shall do so in accordance with law, comprehensively, timely, and in a standardized manner.

Article 2 China Judgments Online is the unified platform for the nationwide publication of adjudicative documents by courts. People's Courts at all levels shall set up links to China Judgments Online on their own government websites and judicial openness platforms.

Article 5 The People's Court shall inform the parties of the scope of publishing adjudicative documents on the Internet in the notice of acceptance of a case and the notice of responding to a lawsuit, and shall inform the public of the relevant provisions on the People's Court's publication of adjudicative documents on the Internet through multiple means such as government websites, electronic touch screens, and litigation guides.

Article 6 For adjudicative documents not published on the Internet, the case number, trial court, date of adjudication, and reasons for non-disclosure shall be published, except where publishing the aforesaid information may disclose state secrets.

Article 7 Adjudicative documents that have taken legal effect shall be published on the Internet within seven working days from the date on which they take effect. For judgments or rulings of first instance that are subjected to a protest or appeal in accordance with law, they shall be published on the Internet within seven working days after the adjudication of second instance takes effect.

Article 12 Where the presiding judge considers that an adjudicative document falls under the circumstance set forth in Item (5) of Article 4 of these Provisions that is inappropriate for publication on the Internet, he/she shall submit a written opinion together with the reasons, which shall be reviewed by the head of the division and then submitted to the responsible vice president for approval.

Article 14 People's Courts at all levels shall rely on information technology to incorporate the disclosure of adjudicative documents into trial process management, reduce the workload of disclosing adjudicative documents, and achieve timely, comprehensive, and convenient publication of adjudicative documents.

Article 15 Adjudicative documents published on the Internet shall be consistent with the original documents, except for the technical processing carried out in accordance with the requirements of these Provisions.
Where the People's Court makes a correction for clerical errors in an adjudicative document, it shall promptly publish the ruling correcting the clerical errors on the Internet.
The presiding judge shall be responsible for the consistency between the adjudicative document published on the Internet and the original adjudicative document, as well as the standardization of the technical processing.

Article 16 Where an adjudicative document published on the Internet is inconsistent with the original adjudicative document or the technical processing is improper, it shall be promptly withdrawn and republished after correction.
Where an adjudicative document published on the Internet is found upon examination to fall under the circumstances listed in Article 4 of these Provisions, it shall be promptly withdrawn and handled in accordance with Article 6 of these Provisions.

Article 17 The Information Technology Service Center of the People's Courts shall be responsible for the operation, maintenance, upgrade, and improvement of China Judgments Online, and shall provide convenience for all sectors of society to lawfully use the adjudicative documents disclosed on that website.
China Judgments Online shall realize the interconnection of adjudicative documents based on the case numbers of the different trial procedures applicable to the cases.

Article 18 These Provisions shall come into force on October 1, 2016. Where any judicial interpretation or normative document previously issued by the Supreme People's Court is inconsistent with these Provisions, these Provisions shall prevail.
